query: Explain the concept of Visual Odometry (VO) and its relationship with the broader Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) framework.
answer:
Visual Odometry (VO) is a process used in computer vision to estimate the motion of a camera in real-time by analyzing the changes in images taken sequentially. It is a critical component of the broader Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) framework, which aims to build a map of an unknown environment while simultaneously keeping track of the agent's location within it. VO contributes to SLAM by providing the motion estimation necessary for the localization aspect, allowing the system to understand how the camera moves through space without relying on external references.
